problem:
Given that for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+3\operatorname{cos}⁡2t$ for $s>0.$

feedback.problem:
Given that for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of  $f(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡3t-5\operatorname{sin}⁡3t$ for $s>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{8\operatorname{cos}⁡3t-5\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} & =L{8\operatorname{cos}⁡3t}+L{-5\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} \\  & =8L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t}-5L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0, \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0 \\ L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =8L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t}-5L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} \\  & =8\cdot \frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}-5\cdot \frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9} \\  & =\frac{8s}{{s}^{2}+9}-\frac{15}{{s}^{2}+9} \\  & =\frac{8s-15}{{s}^{2}+9}.\end{aligned}
$$
